drg.description: Kidney and Urinary Tract Infections without MCC

notes.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL. Patient seen and examined at bedside. 51-year-old female admitted for urinary tract infection. Admission data:
Day 0: labs bilirubin 0.58, creatinine 1.05-1.25, hemoglobin 12.3-12.4, platelets 185-192, sodium 140, wbc 6.9-7; vitals dbp 67-71, heart_rate 85-90, map 87-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 124-129, spo2 96-97, temp 36.8-36.9
Day 0 orders/meds/results: Urinalysis: positive nitrites, >50 WBC/hpf; Ceftriaxone 1 g IV
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension.

PROGRESS NOTE, hospital day 1. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed. Data:
Day 1: labs creatinine 1.51-1.69, hemoglobin 12.4-12.5, platelets 185-186, sodium 140, wbc 6.4-6.5; vitals dbp 68-71, heart_rate 86-91, map 86-90, o2_flow 0, resp_rate 16-17, sbp 123-130, spo2 96-98, temp 36.9-37
Day 1 orders/meds/results: Ceftriaxone 1 g IV; Hold lisinopril; Lactated Ringer's 1 L IV bolus
Assessment and plan: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Continue current management.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY. 51-year-old female, length of stay 4 days. Hospital course: treated per the plan above with daily labs and vital signs; stable for discharge. Medications reconciled and return precautions reviewed. Discharge diagnoses: Urinary tract infection. Hypertension. Follow up with primary care in one week. Patient interviewed and examined; nursing notes reviewed.
